news.title: Argentina were World Cup’s most targeted team online, says FIFA report
news.lede: Argentina were the most targeted national team on social media during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with accusations of referee favouritism, corruption and xenophobia among the main forms of abuse directed at the side, a FIFA report published on October 9 noted. The governing body’s Social Media Protection Service (SMPS) analysed more than 17.1 million posts and comments on X, Instagram, Facebook and TikTok between June 9 and July 20. Of those, 477,000 were referred for human review, with 240,000 verified as abusive. England were the second-most targeted team, followed by Spain, Brazil and Norway, the report found.

news.title: Wales v Albania: Rhian Wilkinson's side hope pattern continues in Women's World Cup play-off semi-final
news.lede: Wales are ranked 31st in the world, 17 places below Norway, who they could face in a play-off final in December. If the pattern of this Women's World Cup qualifying campaign continues, Wales will be starting preparations for a play-off final come Wednesday morning. Wales return home to Llanelli on Tuesday for the second leg of their play-off semi-final with a lead courtesy of a 1-0 triumph in Albania. It was a game which mirrored the three Wales played on their travels during the group stage of this World Cup qualifying campaign, in the Czech Republic, Albania and Montenegro.

news.title: Motsepe: Africa must win World Cup
news.lede: SANTA MARIA: CAF President Patrice Motsepe has challenged African football to turn its growing influence on the world stage into tangible results, declaring that the continent must win the FIFA World Cup. news.title: Lionesses take control of World Cup playoff tie but unfancied Greece still in fight
news.lede: World Cup qualifying playoff: Greece 1-3 England. Stanway, Le Tissier and Russo on target. Sarina Wiegman said she wanted to see a bit more from her side after their fairly underwhelming performance against a hugely unfancied Greek side, despite securing a valuable first-leg victory in their Women’s World Cup playoff tie. Georgia Stanway’s neat finish, Maya Le Tissier’s first England goal and Alessia Russo’s low strike were enough to give England control but a Kallisti Brouksair goal for Greece means that the tie is not definitively over, going into Tuesday’s second leg, and Wiegman acknowledged that England had been “a bit sloppy” at times.
